target_customer: Beginners learning to code on mobile (consumer), later employers screening engineers
problem: Learning to code is hard to start and hard to keep up. Py offered short gamified mobile lessons, then pivoted to skills-based hiring assessments for employers.
business_model: Free consumer app, later B2B assessment subscriptions (Py for Work)
product_category: Mobile coding education, then technical assessments

founders.name: Derek Lo
education: College computer science major (school not stated in the cited source)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (June 2017) says he delayed YC to finish his degree and leads design. It describes him and a friend as first-time founders. The YC page lists no founders, and the second founder's name differs across sources (campus coverage and Crunchbase disagree), so no second founder is listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: A content-driven mobile app with a lesson engine for iOS and Android built by a team of two or three students; the assessment product later needed code execution sandboxes.

defensibility.rationale: Lesson content and a gamified UI were easy to copy, and the app relied on App Store features for downloads.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied the app per sources. The company pivoted into hiring assessments and was bought by Hired in February 2019, which renamed the product Hired Assessments.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported over 100,000 downloads by June 2017 with no concerted marketing, helped by an App Store feature, and about 10 free courses, which shows consumer interest in learning to code on phones.

branding.domain_note: Used getpy.com rather than py.com; no purchase story found.

identity.visual_style: Duolingo style gamified mobile design per TechCrunch

rebrands.why: Product absorbed into the acquirer Hired.

branding.community_and_virality: App Store feature and a Product Hunt launch in September 2016 drove 100,000 plus downloads by mid 2017.

brand_strength.rationale: A very short name that collides with Python and other products in search, with no brand press beyond product launch coverage; traction came from App Store editorial features.

pivots.to: Py for Work, skills-based hiring assessments for employers
pivots.why: Not stated by sources; the product described itself as launching Py for Work to take a skills-based approach to hiring. Exact date not found.

outcome_analysis: Py grew a consumer coding app to over 100,000 downloads by June 2017 on an App Store feature, raised only small amounts, and pivoted to hiring assessments sold to companies like LiveRamp and Amplitude. Hired bought it in February 2019 and turned it into Hired Assessments. The price was undisclosed and funding is thinly documented, so the exit looks like a small strategic or team acquisition.
notes: getpy.com returned HTTP 503 when fetched. Yale Venture Creation Program committed $100K per TechCrunch but terms were not final, so not recorded as a round. Dealroom lists the acquisition as 2021 but VentureBeat and Hired coverage show February 2019. A $120K YC amount in aggregators is unverified. TechCrunch named language apps (Duolingo, Babbel, Verbling) only as analogies, and no dated learn-to-code competitor was found, so the list is empty.
